n: Some of Israel’s elders in exile come and sit before Ezekiel, apparently wanting a word from the Lord.

f.w: elders of Israel

n: God speaks to Ezekiel about these visitors.

f.w: the word of the LORD came unto me
f.g: God reveals what lies behind their outward piety.

n: Outwardly they seek God, but they have set up idols in their hearts. Their inner loyalties trip them up. Should God answer people like that?

f.w: set up their idols in their heart
f.g: An idol can be anything we love or trust more than God.

f.w: stumblingblock
f.g: Something that causes a person to trip and fall into sin.

n: Anyone who comes to a prophet while clinging to heart-idols will get an answer that matches those idols—God will respond to the real condition of their heart.

f.w: according to the multitude of his idols
f.g: In keeping with, or because of, their idols.

n: God’s aim is to “take hold of” Israel’s hearts—to win them back, since their idols have made them strangers to him.

f.w: take the house of Israel in their own heart
f.g: Grip their hearts; confront them inwardly.

f.w: estranged

n: The cure is plain: repent, turn away from your idols, and turn your faces from your abominations.

f.w: Repent, and turn yourselves

n: This applies to Israelites and to foreigners living among them alike. God himself will answer such a person.

f.w: the stranger that sojourneth in Israel
f.g: A resident foreigner, who was also under God’s law.

f.w: I the LORD will answer him by myself
f.g: God will respond directly—with judgment rather than words.

n: God will oppose that person and make him a warning example and a byword, cut off from his people.

f.w: a sign and a proverb

n: If a prophet is drawn into giving such people the comfortable answer they want, God permits that deception and will judge the prophet too. Those who refuse truth may be given over to their own delusions.

f.w: I the LORD have deceived that prophet
f.g: Hebrew idiom: God allows it as judgment.

n: Both the inquirer and the false prophet will bear the same punishment—both chose to prefer lies to truth.

f.w: the punishment of the prophet shall be even as the punishment of him that seeketh unto him

n: The purpose of judgment is restoration: that Israel stops straying, is cleansed, and becomes God’s people again.

f.w: that they may be my people, and I may be their God

n: A new message about whether the righteous can save others.

f.w: The word of the LORD came again to me

n: When a land sins grievously, God may send famine, cutting off both people and animals.

f.w: break the staff of the bread

n: Even if Noah, Daniel, and Job—famous examples of righteousness—lived there, their goodness would save only themselves. Righteousness can’t be transferred to others who refuse to repent.

f.w: Noah, Daniel, and Job
f.g: Noah and Job were ancient righteous men; Daniel was Ezekiel’s contemporary in Babylon, though some scholars think an ancient hero named Danel is meant.

f.w: deliver but their own souls

n: Or if God sends wild animals to depopulate the land so no one can pass through…

f.w: noisome beasts

n: …even these three could not save their own sons or daughters; only they would survive.

f.w: they shall deliver neither sons nor daughters
f.g: In contrast, Noah’s family was saved with him.

n: Or if God commands a sword to sweep through the land…

f.w: Sword, go through the land

n: …the same: only the righteous themselves would be rescued.

f.w: they only shall be delivered themselves
f.g: Each person stands before God for himself.

n: Or if God sends plague and bloodshed…

f.w: pestilence

n: …Noah, Daniel, and Job could only save their own lives by their righteousness. The fourfold repetition drives the point home.

f.w: they shall but deliver their own souls by their righteousness

n: How much worse for Jerusalem, which will face all four judgments together—sword, famine, wild beasts, and plague.

f.w: my four sore judgments

n: Surprisingly, some survivors—sons and daughters—will come out and arrive among the exiles. When the exiles see how wicked they are, they will understand why God judged Jerusalem.

f.w: a remnant that shall be brought forth
ye shall be comforted
f.g: Consoled—by understanding that God acted justly.

n: Seeing the survivors’ conduct, the exiles will know that God did nothing without cause. God’s judgments are never arbitrary.

f.w: I have not done without cause
